verdict: No mixed profile survivor in the requested screen. Granite/Qwen have zero gain against the stronger fixed-width controls. Granite4 has 0.0020665% raw search gain, but remains all-g12, so allowing mixed profiles contributes zero. Do not expand or claim global impossibility from this coordinate-descent screen.
protocol: 32 original train prompts x first64 decode steps. Granite4 first3layers, Granite/Qwen first2layers, both GU/down. No test routes, weights, model inference or VM access.
profiles: All widths1..16, 16cyclicwindows, floor/ceil complete row counts. No width divisibility shortcut. Include wave_template rotations. Every expert retains one complete weight copy; no replication or changed numerical row dot products.
controls: Read and snapshot moe agent matched-budget strong same-g winners. Independently refit fixed-width overlapping cyclic masks and the fixed wave-template family. Mixed seeds include original main, strong same-g, best fixed family and ALL minimum-work fixed-width local optima (including coarse g1), plus wave-template local optima. Every run has the same32-pass cap; all reached a strict coordinate local optimum.
search_budget_caveat: The mixed family receives more total candidate evaluations because its menu and number of starts are larger. This favors detecting mixed gains. A uniform winner is explicitly also a feasible fixed-profile control; its different search path is not credited to mixed geometry. No equal-total-proposal novelty claim is made.
exact_cost: For every proposed whole-row profile recompute per-chip page/wave/run, input presence or expert-specific vector, output rows, channel sums and host transfer. C++ weighted objectives match independent NumPy evaluation over all unique events; scalar selected routes also agree. NAND28us/wave dominates6.4GB/s for <=4pages/wave.
dependence: GU -> host complete-row reassembly/activation -> down remains mandatory. No local activation, free cross-command vector retention, fractional row or new MAC.
g4_down_granularity: Widths3/4/6/12 all have exactly12waves/expert; individual tile grains4/3/2/1 respectively and native commands3/4/6/12. These profiles were included as candidates and as starting families. They did not yield a mixed winning solution.
bound_limit: The saved profile_work_command_relaxation is deliberately optimistic: route-adaptive profiles, ideal aggregate-work balance and no ONFI fanout. It does not enforce indivisible job bin packing or one fixed layout across routes. Its5-wave G4down headroom is NOT a feasible fixed-layout certificate or a no-go proof.
capacity: Final complete-model virtual addresses were reparsed: every tensor row appears once and every chip/plane range is disjoint.20GiB/chip is a research scenario proposed by the coordinating root agent; it is not a direct user constraint or measured hardware capacity. Results also fit if the assumed20GiB is TLC raw. Model useful/16 is a namespace comparison reference, not an equal physical-chip quota. Some block tails grow; reservation is reported separately from payload. Only routed I8 FFN payload is counted; scales/other tensors/FTL are excluded.
no_global_claim: Two-expert block moves, unrestricted masks, global optimization and other layers were not exhausted. The coordinating root agent set a below1% screening gate for this branch; this was not a human instruction to stop research. The observed attributable mixed-profile gain is zero.
